did: read the muster before Davout's attack
expected: a plain statement of why Davout fights at a penalty

did: read the enemy phase report for turn 1
expected: a report whose moves match the map

did: fought two battles and ended turn 1 with 432 gold showing
expected: a warning before End Turn that upkeep exceeds income, or a treasury that survives the first turn
saw: Turn 2 opens at -54 gold: 'Upkeep -3644g ... Net -486g', 'Treasury in deficit!'. Nothing told me before I ended the turn that the army's upkeep outruns income, nor that each battle burns gold as 'materiel'. did: opened the 'Bernadotte — free attack!' card in the Imperial Box
expected: a free attack only after a win
saw: 'Bernadotte earned a free attack from his defensive victory' — but the enemy phase and the diorama both said Bernadotte was ROUTED, 'THE FIELD IS LOST', forced to retreat with 8,135 left and -30% effectiveness. Offering a broken corps a 'free' strike on 50,000 men looks like a trap

expected: the muster to warn that Lannes would leave Bohemia, or Lannes to stay since he was guarding a fresh conquest
saw: 'WILL JOIN — Lannes: marches to the sound of the guns' and after the battle every joining corps (Lannes, Ney, Davout, Massena, Napoleon, Teulie) now stands in Tyrol; Bohemia is left empty. expected: both answers, or at least the first
saw: again a two-part question defeats Berthier: 'I cannot answer that from the dispatches, Sire.' The single question 'where is Lannes' worked at once

did: looked at the Imperial Box rail with 5,129 gold in the treasury
expected: the deficit warning to clear once the treasury recovered
saw: the 'Treasury in deficit' icon still sits first on the rail on turns 3 and 4, long after the treasury went positive (2,654 then 5,129). Also, a gold offer from an accepted open-borders treaty did not show in the Gold counter until a later click

did: clicked Counter on Austria's armistice offer, after taking Vienna, intending to ask for a real peace
expected: a form where I choose my counter-terms before anything is sent
saw: Counter sent terms I never saw or chose: 'Talleyrand attempted to negotiate, but Austria found our counter-terms unacceptable. The proposal is rejected. (1 DP spent)'. The envoy is gone and a diplomatic point spent; also the offer still showed the stale war score 58 although Vienna's fall had raised it to +80

did: read 'Press Austria alone: the separate peace. It costs 3 diplomatic points' in the settlement window and clicked the [Press Austria] button
expected: a separate peace with Austria
saw: the button means 'demand more of Austria': it added 'Cede Carniola' and Austria fell from 12/50 to -17/50 ('settlement dial harsher'). The advice text and the button share the word 'Press' but do different things

did: reviewed the white peace with Austria before ratifying, wanting to keep Vienna
expected: one clear statement of who keeps the occupied provinces
saw: 'no terms exchanged, no map redrawn — only the war ends' next to 'Vienna stays ours by this treaty', and the demand list offered no 'keep Vienna' line. Only after ratifying did it say 'Status quo: Bohemia, Tyrol and Vienna stay ours'. I ratified half-guessing

expected: an attack with the muster, or a refusal saying Moravia is not adjacent to Bohemia
saw: the order silently became a 2-AP PURSUE standing order: 'Ney pursues Kutuzov (at Moravia). Moves to Dresden.' Ney walked alone into neutral Saxony, away from the army, and I lost half my turn's actions. Nothing asked me first or showed the route

did: recruited 3,000 infantry for Bernadotte
expected: a consistent morale report
saw: 'Morale: 21% -> 26%' followed by '[WARNING] Morale dropped to 26% — consider drilling'. Morale rose, the warning says it dropped; and nothing earlier told me Bernadotte's corps sat at 21% morale

did: with Davout, Soult, Napoleon and Massena stacked in Vienna, ordered 'Massena, attack Kutuzov' in Moravia
expected: the muster as a preview I could cancel, or the attack refused, when the others could not join
saw: the attack went ahead at once with Massena alone ('the balance of force looks unfavorable'; Davout/Soult/Napoleon 'cannot march — the field is on soil we are not at war with'). Moravia is Austrian and I had just made peace with Austria — the Russians stand there safe from my combined army, but Massena alone may still attack in. Lost 6,243 men for 1,861; nothing warned me the peace walled off Moravia

did: ordered 'Davout, fortify Vienna' with 2 AP left, expecting it to cost 1 (as the battle text had said 'fortify him (1 AP)')
expected: 1 AP, or a question before it took 2
saw: '[Auto-shifted to DEFENSIVE stance first — cost 2 AP: 1 for stance change + 1 for fortify]' — both my remaining actions gone without asking

did: reviewed Britain's settlement offer
expected: the offer's headline ('Britain retains Leon') to match the terms shown on review, and the score to agree with 'carries'
saw: the envoy card said 'Status quo: Britain retains Leon', but the review lists only 'End hostilities (no material change)' and 'no map redrawn'; and 'Britain — Their own terms (11/50)' sits beside 'This peace carries'. I could not tell if my ally Spain loses Leon

did: assaulted the 3,000-man Silesia garrison with Soult (19k), Soult again, Massena (19k), then ordered Davout (18k) in
expected: a 19,000-man corps to take a 3,000-man post in one assault
saw: each assault only halved the garrison (3,000 -> 1,500 -> 750 -> 375), costing 3 actions; then Davout objected 'Sire, the enemy is too strong. We need reinforcements' against 375 men, and overruling him cost -8 trust — after which the 375 simply laid down their arms. Nothing told me how small a garrison must be before it yields

action_text: type where are Ney, Lannes, Massena and Napoleon

expected: the leader and his supports to end the battle in the same place

expected: a sweeter offer to raise Prussia's willingness
saw: it added 'France pays 100 gold' and Prussia fell from 14/50 to 8/50, now saying 'the terms claim a victory the field has not delivered' — paying them made the peace less acceptable, the opposite of what the advice promised

did: Lannes was 'cornered at Brandenburg ... capture looms' and I chose 'Attempt a Breakout' over 'Fight to the Last'
expected: to be told whether the breakout worked, and where Lannes went
saw: no result line at all — the battle diorama replayed the earlier defeat, and only by typing 'status' did I learn 'PRISONERS: Lannes: held by Prussia at Berlin since T13'. A marshal lost without the game ever telling me the breakout failed or what the odds were

did: the Balance of Europe said 'Saxony ... The price to keep her out: Talleyrand brings her to -10 in 2 turns (2 DP)', so I opened Saxony in the Diplomacy window to do it

did: retook Vienna and Bohemia — provinces Austria had already ceded to me by treaty, which Russia had seized the turn before

did: pressed Escape to close the Generals screen (also earlier the Ledger and Diplomatic Ledger)
